title: RRB Technician answer key 2026: Grade I and III objection deadline is 22 October
summary: RRB’s 15 October notices publish the Technician Grade I Signal and Grade III response-sheet/key windows. The scheduled objection deadline is 22 October 2026 at 11:55 PM.
cycle: Technicians CEN 02/2026 · Grade I Signal and Grade III

facts.label: Objection fee
facts.value: ₹50 plus applicable bank service charges per question

sections.title: Use the right grade’s response sheet
sections.body: The two official notices share a viewing and challenge window but have separate candidate links. Grade I Signal and Grade III candidates must use their own grade. This is Technician CEN 02/2026, not ALP CEN 01/2026; an ALP application does not make the Technician key relevant to you.

sections.title: Challenge a question before the published deadline
sections.body: The notices set the viewing, objection and payment window from 15 October at 16:00 to 22 October at 23:55. The fee is ₹50 plus bank service charges per question. If an objection is accepted, the valid-objection fee is refunded after applicable charges to the account used for payment. A provisional key may change; the response-sheet raw score is not a normalised result.

nextSteps: Open the matching Grade I or Grade III notice and confirm CEN 02/2026.
Use the corresponding official candidate link to save your question paper, recorded responses and key while access is available.

Submit supported objections through the official tracker and complete payment within the published window. If it has ended, check for an official extension rather than assuming late submissions are accepted.

title: UP Police Constable final result: 2025 recruitment selection list published
summary: UPPRPB published the final selection result on 14 October 2026 for Advertisement 07/2025. The notice also confirms PET completion from 1 to 11 October.

facts.label: Recruitment
facts.value: Constable Civil Police and equivalent posts

sections.title: Which recruitment does this cover?
sections.body: This notice belongs to the direct recruitment advertised on 31 December 2025 as Advertisement 07/2025. The written examination and physical stages took place during 2026. Match the advertisement number when checking a result; a calendar year in a headline is not enough to identify the recruitment.

sections.title: What changed after the physical tests?
sections.body: The final-result notice records the completed PET window as 1–11 October, after centre-specific schedule changes. It supersedes the original shorter window. Final selection uses normalised written-examination merit with the applicable reservation and preference rules; passing PET alone does not identify a candidate as selected.

nextSteps: Open the board’s final-result notice and confirm Advertisement 07/2025.
Use the final-result lookup linked from uppbpb.gov.in and match your own candidate details.
Save your result and follow the board’s subsequent instructions for verification, medical requirements and appointment.

title: SBI PO mains result 2026: shortlist out, Phase 3 dates announced
summary: SBI has published its mains shortlist for CRPD/PO/2026-27/09. Tentative next dates are 31 October for the psychometric test and interviews from 18 November.

facts.label: Call letters
facts.value: Exact date and time to follow in call letters

sections.title: How to read the result
sections.body: The official PDF is a roll-number shortlist for the next stage. Search using the roll number from your own mains call letter and check every digit. This is not a final appointment list. SBI publishes candidate marks separately, so absence of an individual scorecard is not evidence that the roll-number PDF is incomplete.

sections.title: What happens in Phase 3?
sections.body: SBI’s separate notice gives tentative dates for the psychometric test, Group Exercise and interviews. It says call letters with the exact date and time will be released shortly. Candidates should use their assigned appointment rather than assuming that everyone attends on the first interview date. The publication date of the mains PDF was not established in this review.

nextSteps: Open the official mains PDF and search for your exact roll number.
Read the Phase 3 notice and keep the registration login and original certificates ready.
Check the matching PO advertisement on SBI careers for your call letter and any revised appointment.

title: SSC GD result 2026 declared: PET/PST shortlist and official cutoff notice
summary: SSC’s 12 October result write-up shortlists CBT candidates for PET/PST. CRPF will issue physical-test call letters and dates separately.
cycle: SSC Constable GD / Rifleman GD Examination 2026

facts.label: PET/PST dates
facts.value: To be issued separately; not fixed by this result notice

sections.title: What the result means
sections.body: Candidates on the relevant shortlist may proceed to the physical-test stage subject to the notice’s conditions. The CBT shortlist is not final force allocation or appointment. Use the correct gender and vacancy scope when consulting the candidate lists and cutoff annexures.

sections.title: Why there is no single nationwide cutoff
sections.body: The write-up contains state/UT and area-specific cutoff annexures with category and gender distinctions, plus a separate SSF table. Comparing your score to an unrelated row can give the wrong conclusion. The notice directs shortlisted candidates to CRPF for PET/PST call letters; individual marks and final answer keys are to be made available by SSC in due course.

nextSteps: Read the SSC result write-up and locate the candidate list that applies to you.
Match the correct state/UT, area, category, gender and force scope before reading a cutoff.
Check CRPF recruitment for your physical-test call letter and instructions; keep the required certificates ready.

title: SSC CHSL 2025 final result declared: official selection and allocation notice
summary: SSC declared the CHSL 2025 final result on 7 October 2026 after the allocation and identity-verification process. This result is separate from CHSL 2026.

facts.label: CHSL 2026
facts.value: Separate recruitment; this is not its result

sections.title: Check the cycle before your roll number
sections.body: SSC’s final-result notice concerns the 2025 examination, although the notice was published in October 2026. Candidates registered for CHSL 2026 should follow their own examination schedule instead. Mixing those cycles can make an application appear to have a result before its examination has taken place.

sections.title: How allocation affects the final result
sections.body: The write-up explains the outcome after the tentative allocation and subsequent sliding/identity-verification process. It gives post-wise and category-wise allocation and cutoff details. Read the conditions and the relevant candidate list, rather than treating an isolated cutoff screenshot as proof of selection.

nextSteps: Open the SSC final-result write-up and verify that it says CHSLE 2025.
Check your roll number and the applicable post/category details in the official result material.
Follow the user department’s document-verification and appointment instructions, keeping your application and certificates ready.

title: SSC Havaldar additional result 2025: PET/PST shortlist notice published
summary: SSC published an additional Havaldar shortlist on 7 October 2026. The write-up includes withheld-candidature and sealed-cover conditions; it is not an MTS final result.
cycle: MTS and Havaldar Examination 2025 · Havaldar additional CBT result

facts.label: Important distinction
facts.value: Additional shortlist, not final MTS selection

sections.title: Who should read this additional notice?
sections.body: This write-up follows the original CBT result and concerns the processing of previously unprocessed Havaldar candidature. It does not announce a fresh application cycle. Candidates should check the additional list and conditions rather than assuming the whole MTS/Havaldar result has been replaced.

sections.title: Why the conditions matter
sections.body: The notice distinguishes shortlisted candidates whose candidature remains withheld from separate sealed-cover cases. Appearing on an additional list must not be described as unconditional clearance or final selection. Read the complete write-up alongside the original result conditions and follow any candidate-specific official instructions.

nextSteps: Open the additional-result write-up dated 7 October and confirm that it applies to your candidature.
Check the additional candidate list and the exact withheld or sealed-cover conditions.
Follow the official PET/PST instructions for your case; do not substitute an unofficial final-result claim.

title: SSC CHSL 2026 Tier 1 dates: exam window set for 30 November–31 December
summary: SSC’s 1 October schedule places CHSL 2026 Tier 1 between 30 November and 31 December. Candidates will receive their individual date and shift separately.

facts.label: Tier 2
facts.value: Not confirmed in this schedule notice

sections.title: What SSC has announced
sections.body: The schedule gives a date window for the computer-based Tier 1 examination. It does not assign every applicant the same date or announce that admission certificates are already downloadable. Check the candidate-specific date, shift, reporting time and centre when SSC publishes that information.

sections.title: How to use the preparation gap
sections.body: Application and correction windows have closed. Use the remaining weeks for timed sectional practice, complete mocks and daily typing practice. Separate the 2026 examination from the CHSL 2025 final result published in October: the older result does not change your 2026 application status.

nextSteps: Save the SSC schedule and note the full Tier 1 window.
Check SSC’s candidate account and noticeboard for your individual city/date information and admission certificate.
Confirm your own reporting time and any later schedule revision before arranging travel.

title: IBPS Clerk CSA-XVI mains 2026: official calendar lists 27 December
summary: The IBPS 2026–27 tentative calendar lists CSA-XVI mains for 27 December 2026. Result and call-letter availability must be checked separately.
cycle: CRP Customer Service Associates XVI · 2026–27 exam calendar

facts.label: This update
facts.value: Calendar clarification, not a new result release

sections.title: This corrects the date on our guide
sections.body: Our earlier guide used a 6 December estimate. The official IBPS calendar instead lists CSA-XVI mains on 27 December. This article is a clarification of the calendar published on 16 January, not a claim that IBPS issued a new October examination notice.

sections.title: Keep calendar dates separate from release status
sections.body: IBPS reserves the right to change the tentative examination dates. A scheduled date does not establish that a result or call letter is available, nor does it establish that an examination was completed without changes. Use the current CSA-XVI page and your own call letter for candidate-specific instructions.

nextSteps: Use 27 December as the tentative mains planning date, subject to later IBPS changes.
Check the CSA-XVI cycle page for the actual prelims-result and mains-call-letter announcement.
Continue mains preparation while waiting; confirm your assigned date and reporting time from the call letter when issued.

title: RRB NTPC UG CBT 2 answer key: CEN 07/2025 window and next steps
summary: The official notice for the 17 September 2026 CBT 2 set its response-sheet and objection window for 24–30 September. That published window has ended; this is not a new open challenge period.

facts.label: Objection fee in notice
facts.value: ₹50 plus applicable bank service charges per question

sections.title: Which NTPC cycle is this?
sections.body: This notice covers the undergraduate recruitment under CEN 07/2025. It is separate from graduate NTPC and the new 2026 application cycles. The notice concerns CBT 2 held on 17 September, not a key for an examination that has not yet taken place.

sections.title: What remains useful after the window?
sections.body: The notice is a record of how responses and provisional keys were made available. Its listed objection period has passed. Use a response sheet you saved for analysis and watch the official RRB portal for later result or revised-key information; this article does not establish a new download window or an extension.

nextSteps: Confirm that your application says CEN 07/2025 undergraduate and that you appeared in CBT 2.
Use the official notice as the record of the closed 24–30 September window.
Follow the unified RRB portal for subsequent result and selection-stage notices. Do not submit payment to an unofficial late-objection service.

title: RRB Group D answer key: CEN 09/2025 response-sheet window has ended
summary: RRB’s official notice covered the 3–25 August 2026 Level-1 CBT. The published key and objection window ran from 7 September, 8 PM, to 17 September, 11:55 PM.

facts.label: Objection fee in notice
facts.value: ₹50 plus applicable bank service charges per question

sections.title: The official notice resolves the CBT end date
sections.body: The key notice identifies the CBT window as 3–25 August 2026. That is the window used here in place of conflicting secondary summaries. This is CEN 09/2025; notices for the earlier CEN 08/2024 recruitment belong to a different cycle.

sections.title: After a provisional key
sections.body: A provisional response sheet helps calculate raw marks and identify potential key errors. It does not establish qualification, a rank or the normalised score used for shortlisting. The published challenge window has ended. Check the unified RRB portal for subsequent announcements rather than relying on a result date inferred from the key release.

nextSteps: Match CEN 09/2025 before using any Group D key or result notice.
Keep the response sheet and payment receipt if you saved them during the published window.
Check the official portal for the next result/PET notice; the key notice is not proof that a result has been declared.

title: RRB Group D CCAA modification window: 22–28 October for eligible apprentices
summary: RRB has announced a restricted CCAA modification window under CEN 09/2025 for NCVT marks and certificate details. It is not a fresh application opportunity for all candidates.
cycle: Level-1 CEN 09/2025 · eligible Course Completed Act Apprentices

facts.label: Who it covers
facts.value: Eligible CCAA candidates described in the official notice

facts.label: Purpose
facts.value: NCVT marks and certificate details; not new general applications

sections.title: Who should check this notice?
sections.body: The facility is for the CCAA cases described by RRB under CEN 09/2025, including candidates who appeared in CBT and had not furnished their NCVT marks in the application. The notice links the eligibility condition to having appeared in the NCVT examination before the original application deadline. Read the full conditions before assuming that an apprentice claim qualifies.

sections.title: Why the modification matters
sections.body: The notice explains how the certificate details and NCVT marks enable calculation of the applicable CCAA weightage. It warns about missing marks and representations outside the modification window. This facility is separate from the earlier answer-key objection tracker and does not reopen applications for all Group D candidates.

nextSteps: Read the CCAA notice and confirm that your application falls within its stated conditions.
Use the modification link reached from the official unified RRB portal during the scheduled 22–28 October window.
Check the NCVT certificate details and marks carefully, submit the required changes and save the acknowledgement.
